items.evidence: The first section after the title is '## The bottom line', whose three paragraphs open '**1. What FRUS answers directly.**', '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**' and '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**' in that order; 'Scope' and 'Decisions this needs from you' follow them and '## Findings' comes only after. The collection's introductionText repeats the same three parts in the same order ('What FRUS answers directly: across the 553 volumes indexed…', then 'Where FRUS points for the rest:', then 'What this request cannot get from FRUS:').

No '%' or 'percent' anywhere in the overview. Every figure carries its set in words: 'about eleven hundred documents in 123 volumes pair the word recognition with a coup…', 'nine times in ten among those that carry a source line', 'one document in twenty carries such a footnote', 'about one document in six of the vocabulary-defined set (187 of 1,131)', 'about six and a half documents in every thousand dated documents of that decade', '37 of the 186 documents of 1943–1951', '255 of its 25,115 sections', 'Eighty-four documents were retrieved whole and fifty-three are quoted'. Weakest spots, none a bare figure: 'under Kennedy (19 of 114)' names its base only as a number until a later paragraph says 'the 114 of 1961–1968'; 'the eight-in-ten line' is a threshold, not a count; and 'Read next' says 'the fifty-eight documents above' when the overview cites fifty-three (the collection holds fifty-eight, five of them with a note but no excerpt and no citation above: 1881 d583, 1936 v05 d107, 1943 v05 d484, 1947 v08 d755, 1964–68 v31 d209).

Sixty 'Document N' citations and sixty history.state.gov links, 53 distinct documents, every one present in the collection; a grep for 'frus' outside 'historicaldocuments/' finds nothing, so no bare id pair, and nothing is cited by title alone. Full form throughout, e.g. '(Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1945, The American Republics, Volume IX, Document 242, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1945v09/d242)' and '(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1958–1960, Volume V, Microfiche Supplement, American Republics, Document VE–1, https://…/frus1958-60v05mSupp/ve_d1)'. Weak point: eleven short forms '(Document N, link)' after a full citation of the same volume, and three of them follow a full citation of a DIFFERENT volume — '(Document 1138, https://…/frus1944v07/d1138)' and '(Document 1170, https://…/frus1945v09/d1170)' in Finding 5 after the 1945 Volume IX citation, and '(Document 109, https://…/frus1961-63v10-12mSupp/d109)' in Finding 6 after Volume XII citations — so on paper their volume is read only from the link's path.

The decisive passage is the fourth part: 'the one South America volume indexed for the decade holds nineteen documents that use the word recognition and nine that mention a coup, but none that pairs them, while the control phrase ‘Department of State’ returns sixty-nine, so the absence is the volume's and not the search's'. The first part gives terms, scope and a control: 'the search for recognition near ‘treaty of peace and amity’, ‘1923 treaty’ or ‘article II’ (168 documents in the whole index, 65 in the set) finds only discussion and one quotation of the article … (one document of the 178 in that volume that name the Department)'; the third gives terms and counts: 'the Tobar, Estrada and Betancourt doctrines appear in 29 documents in the whole index, 16 in the set, always as reported by American officers … (four footnotes in the scope volumes cite one)'. Shortfall: the second part names no terms — 'the search for a coup-policy phrase near recognition in the three Kennedy and Johnson volumes for the region returned eleven documents, every one a country case' — identifies its volumes only by description and has no control, so it is the one absence the historian could not repeat; judged yes because every absence is stated as a run search with its counts, the zero that is a zero (1981–1988) carries its control, and the policy-paper result is eleven documents read rather than a bare zero.

No SQL keyword, no underscore identifier, no table or column name and no file path in the overview (case-sensitive scan; 'documents', 'volumes', 'sections' and 'index' occur only as English words: '255 of its 25,115 sections', 'the index folds ‘recognize’, ‘recognized’ and ‘recognition’ into one stem'). The strings 'frus…/d…' occur only inside the sixty history.state.gov links that J3 requires; the memo is referred to by name ('see the memo for every count'), not by path; the central-file classes are given in words ('the file classes for a country's political affairs and its government, such as Mexico's political affairs, Haiti's, Bolivia's and El Salvador's government class'). The collection's introduction does print '812.00' and '816.01', which are archival file classes rather than database fields, and J5 is about the overview.

score:r7.notes: All four files are present (memo.md 134 lines, overview.md 54, queries.log 156, collection.fruscollection 868), plus out/ (62 files), raw/ (84 dumps), scripts/ (20) and an empty refuter/. Verification performed read-only against the copy: M1, M20, M21, M14, M15 and the M5 decade denominators reproduce exactly from the memo's SQL; M24's Ed2 handling is correct (frus1951-54Iran and frus1969-76ve15p2 first editions exist, no frus1977-80v09 does); core_set.tsv recounts to 3,136 / A 1,131 / B 2,263 / A∩B 258 / 123 volumes / 63 distinct (volume, heading) pairs; all 53 quoted documents and all 58 collection documents are in the 84-line reading log; every overview quotation is a substring of a quotes.tsv text and 14 re-checked with instr() on body_text; Lot 65 D 438 → NAID 27022950 and Lot 81D64 → 27499857 are confirmed in central-files-index.json and series-facts-index.json with the stated extents and years. The three violations: I2 and I3 both rest on the same two exploratory queries (queries.log lines 14 and 120) that correlate frus_documents with document_cache by `rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM document_cache …)`; no reported number depends on them, every join behind a reported figure is on the (volume_id, document_id) pair, and the FTS table is external-content over document_cache (content_rowid='rowid'), so an adjudicator who reads a rowid semi-join as outside 'join' would move I3 to obeyed — I scored the rule as written. O2 fails on a single count: the overview says three footnote passages were dropped where M19 lists six found to be editorial (five post-1960); the other ~50 overview numbers trace to the memo and the trace table is otherwise thorough. Minor points not scored as violations: M1 claims apparatus is excluded 'from every count below unless said otherwise' but the stem and control counts in M14, M15, M20 and M21 are unfiltered without saying so (M14's 19 and 9 do not move with the filter, checked); the overview's 'some two thousand two hundred further documents' counts all 2,263 heading documents though 258 of them are also in the vocabulary set (B-only is 2,005); frus1877/d207 is among the 84 dumps but appears in no memo episode; the memo's '1861–1908: 187' is presented in the overview as 'the 1860s to 1900s' (the decade table sums to 192 for those decades) with the trace table naming the period row explicitly; the memo notes its own 1940s denominator (75,872) differs from a quoted house figure (74,043) and gives the reproducible query, which the scorer confirmed. P5 was scored on the memo; the overview's 'nine times in ten' and 'one document in twenty' are ratios in words whose numbers are in M8 and M9, which O2 rather than P5 governs.

refute:r7.fabricationDetails: None. overview.md holds 57 straight-double-quoted passages (no block quotes: grep '^>' = 0; none contains an ellipsis mark, so each is one segment) and the collection holds 54 excerpts. refuter/quote_check.py lower-cased each, dropped everything but [a-z0-9], and required it as a substring of header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact (volume_id, document_id) the overview's following history.state.gov URL names: 57 of 57 found, and for every one the URL's pair equals the pair the memo's trace gives for its Q-number (Q1–Q54 in out/quotes.tsv; the two d894, two d1028, two d375, two d312, two d363 and two d348 passages are sub-quotes of one excerpt each). All 54 excerpts are found in their cited pair by the same rule and are also exact byte substrings of body_text (54 of 54). One quality defect that the rule does not catch: the frus1945v09/d242 excerpt (Q30) carries the sentence 'For documentation on United States concern with respect to Axis activity in Argentina, see pp. 437 ff.', which the volume XML shows is an editorial <note> flattened into body_text, between items (ii) and (iii); 53 of the 54 excerpts sit entirely in the TEI text with every <note> removed, this one does not (refuter/tei_check_all.py). The memo's M19 says none of the pre-1960 excerpts contains such a 'See …' fragment; that is false for Q30. The overview's own quotation from d242 ('(iii) Termination of the state of siege …') is document text. The 15 single-curly-quoted strings in the overview (‘treaty of peace and amity’, ‘article II’, ‘Department of State’, ‘recognize’ … and the collection's title) are search terms and titles, not document quotations, and were not counted.
refute:r7.miscitationDetails: None. Every quotation is credited to the pair the memo's trace names and is found there. All 60 printed citations with a URL were parsed: the document number agrees with the URL's id in every case (including 'Document VE–1' for ve_d1), and the 11 short-form citations ('Document 227, URL' etc.) resolve to the volume of the preceding citation. 23 of the 60 print the conventional short title 'Foreign Relations of the United States, <year>[, Part/Volume]' where the manifest title is the long 'Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, With the Annual Message … <year>'; each resolves unambiguously (year, part or volume match the volume id), so these are a title convention, not mis-citations. The 37 others match the manifest title character for character after normalisation.

(2) presidential-library-catalog.json: Kennedy NSF (collection NAID 1164) series 'Country Files' 193236, 1961–1963 ✓; Johnson NSF (567979) series 'Latin America Country Files' 567985, 1963–1969 ✓; Nixon 'National Security Files (Nixon Administration)' collection 572235 ✓ — the collection row has no dates; '1969–1974' is its series' span (Institutional, Central Files, Telcons 1969–1974; HAK Office Files 1969–1975); Carter 'Records of the Office of the National Security Advisor' (560131) series 'Zbigniew Brzezinski's Country Files' 560151, 1977–1981 ✓; the catalogue carries no access field for any of these, as the overview says. (3) central-files-index.json lotFiles (1,070 rows) + series-facts-index.json byNaId: 65D438 → naId 27022950, entry A1 3053, RG 59, 1962-1963, Restricted - Partly (FOIA b1), Executive Secretariat, 6 ft 2 in ✓; 53D26 → 2108774, A1 1130, 1949-1953, Unrestricted, ARA ✓; 59D573 → 2108779, A1 1135, 1957-1959, Unrestricted ✓; 57D295 → 2108778, A1 1134, 1953-1956, Unrestricted ✓; 60D665 → 2660902, A1 5474A, 1951-1960, Unrestricted, Office of Inter-American Regional Political Affairs ✓; 66D95 → 2839192, A1 1586E, 1947-1979, Restricted - Partly ✓; 81D113 → 1487627, P 14, 1975-1981, Restricted - Partly, Office of the Deputy Secretary ✓; 81D64 → 27499857, UD-14D 61, 1978-1981, Restricted - Fully ✓; every reference unit 'National Archives at College Park - Textual Reference' ✓. Note the overview's lot names are the FRUS editors' (collection-authority names such as 'S/S Files: Lot 65 D 438', 'OAS Files, Lot 60 D 665'); NARA's series titles differ (65 D 438 'Records Relating to the Cuban Missile Crisis'; 60 D 665 'Records Relating to the Inter-American Cultural Council and the Committee for Cultural Action'; 57 D 295 'Reviews of Foreign Operations Missions'), which the overview does not say. All eight lots do rank in the volume-scope channels for the 123 volumes as the memo states (usage index: 65D438 51 notes in 4 vols, 81D113 40 in 4, 53D26 39 in 3, 57D295 34 in 3, 60D665 29 in 4, 59D573 26 in 2, 81D64 17 in 2, 66D95 7 in 3; external-citation index: 81D113 47 in 3, 81D64 39 in 1, 60D665 34 in 5, 66D95 30 in 5, 57D295 24 in 3, 53D26 24 in 3, 59D573 17 in 2, 65D438 15 in 1; 72 of the 123 scope volumes are in that index, none before frus1911). (4) The claim that the bundle gives the Central Decimal File no identifier, extent or access: confirmed — collection-authority rows 'Central Files', 'Decimal Central Files', 'Central Decimal File 1910–1929', 'Central Files 1964–66' etc. all have naId null; the usage index's top collection for the scope is txt:department of state|central file (1,881 notes in 14 volumes) with none. 3. WRONG OR LOOSE STATEMENTS FOUND (none among the five headline numbers): (a) Paragraph 2: 'Documents before 1910 carry no source line at all' is FALSE. Core documents dated before 1910 = 259; 233 have no document_sources row but 26 DO (frus1907p2 ×11, frus1908 ×5, frus1910 ×4, frus1907p1 ×3, frus1909 ×1 — all 'File No. nnnn/nn' Numerical File citations classed citation_era='decimal' — and frus1865p3/d577, frus1870/d294 classed 'unrecognized'). The memo's M8 (263 without, 233 of them pre-1910) is right; M12's sentence 'The 233 pre-1910 core documents have no source line' is the slip the overview copied. (b) Paragraph 3 / M16: 'the search for a coup-policy phrase near recognition in the three Kennedy and Johnson volumes … returned eleven documents'. The memo's stated query, MATCH 'NEAR(coup* polic*, 12) AND recogn*' AND volume_id IN (frus1961-63v12, frus1961-63v10-12mSupp, frus1964-68v31), returns 5 (d416, d664, d165, d72, d543); the other six the memo lists (d427, d64, d184, d344, d373, d236) are the result of a different query in the log (line 139: recogn* AND (coup OR junta OR 'de facto') AND (policy OR criteria OR doctrine) with header filters); the union is 11. The count is not what the named search returned. The qualitative half ('every one a country case') holds for the 11 as listed (d236 is a Cuba-chapter briefing paper; d344 a Dominican policy directive). (c) Paragraph 3: 'the Tobar, Estrada and Betancourt doctrines appear in 29 documents in the whole index, 16 in the set' — the query (M18) names only Estrada and Tobar; adding NEAR(betancourt doctrine, 20) gives 32 corpus-wide (3 Betancourt documents, 1 of them in the set → 17). (d) Decisions: 'the 1860s to 1900s hold … (187 of 1,131)' — 187 is the 1861–1908 period; the decades 1860s–1900s hold 192 (five documents dated 1909: frus1909/d283, frus1910/d852, d854, d855, d856). Both are about one in six. (e) 'some two thousand two hundred further documents' — 2,263 under the headings, but 258 are already in the vocabulary set; further = 2,005. (f) The frus1945v09/d242 excerpt embeds an editorial footnote sentence (see fabricationDetails); the memo's M19 claim that no pre-1960 excerpt holds a 'See …' fragment is false for it. (g) 'nine times in ten … from the Department's Central Decimal File': 61 of the 2,660 'decimal'-era rows are 1906–1910 Numerical File citations with no decimal class (RG 59 still); 90.5% without them. (h) Nixon 572235 '1969–1974' is a series date; the collection row has none and one series runs to 1975. (i) 'Read next': 'the fifty-eight documents above' — 53 are cited above, 5 are context-only. (j) 23 of 60 printed citations use a short conventional title where the manifest has the long 'Papers Relating to…' form; all resolve.
